title: Common product blowup for flattenings on a finite affine cover
statement: Let $T$ be a quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme, $U\subseteq T$ a quasi-compact open, and $g:W\to T$ a quasi-compact quasi-separated morphism [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions, def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism]. Fix a finite affine open cover $W=\bigcup_{i=1}^r W_i$. For each $i$ let $\mathcal I_i\subseteq\mathcal O_T$ be a finite-type quasi-coherent ideal [pqf-def-coherent] with $\mathcal I_i|_U=\mathcal O_U$, and put $b_i:T_i=\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I_i}(T)\to T$ [def-nagata-global-blowup, def-nagata-admissible-blowup]. Suppose the strict transform $W_i^{(i)}\to T_i$ of $W_i\to T$, relative to the complement of $V(\mathcal I_i)$ [def-nagata-strict-transform], is flat and locally of finite presentation [def-weil-flat-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Put $\mathcal I=\prod_i\mathcal I_i$, $T^b=\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I}(T)$ and $\mathcal J_i=\prod_{k\ne i}\mathcal I_k$, with empty products equal to the unit ideal. Then $T^b\to T$ is a $U$-admissible blowup. For each $i$ it factors through $b_i$ by a blowup $q_i:T^b\to T_i$ in the extended ideal $\mathcal J_i\mathcal O_{T_i}$, where extension means the ideal generated by the image of the pullback of $\mathcal J_i$. This factorization satisfies $V(\mathcal I)=V(\mathcal I_i)\cup b_i(V(\mathcal J_i\mathcal O_{T_i}))$. The strict transform $W_i^{\mathcal I}$ of $W_i$ for $\mathcal I$ is canonically isomorphic to $W_i^{(i)}\times_{T_i}T^b$, compatibly with its inclusion into $W_i\times_T T^b$ and its projections [def-pc-fibre-product]. These $W_i^{\mathcal I}$ are an open cover of the strict transform $W^{\mathcal I}$ of $W$ for $\mathcal I$. The morphism $W^{\mathcal I}\to T^b$ is flat, locally of finite presentation, quasi-compact and quasi-separated, hence of finite presentation. No density of $U$ in $T$ is assumed.

proof.text: On an affine open, generators of a product ideal are products of generators of its factors; thus $\mathcal I$ and every $\mathcal J_i$ are finite-type quasi-coherent ideals. Restriction to $U$ gives the unit ideal. Since $U$ is quasi-compact and $T$ is quasi-separated, the open immersion $U\hookrightarrow T$ is quasi-compact by clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence], as [def-nagata-admissible-blowup] requires. The data for $T^b\to T$ therefore satisfy [def-nagata-admissible-blowup]. For fixed $i$, write $\mathcal I=\mathcal I_i\mathcal J_i$. Apply [thm-nagata-blowup-product-ideal], with the iterated blowup of [def-nagata-blowup-product-comparison], to identify $T^b$ with the blowup of $T_i$ in $\mathcal J_i\mathcal O_{T_i}$. This supplies $q_i$ with $b_iq_i=b$. Extension of a finite list of generators is again a finite list of generators. The case $r=0$ has $W=\varnothing$, the unit-ideal blowup is $T$, and all covering and finiteness conclusions are vacuous or identities.

source.place: Tag 080A, lemma-blowing-up-two-ideals; flat.tex Tag 081R, finite affine-cover reduction

proof.text: We check the support hypothesis needed for composition. Prime ideals contain $\mathcal I_i\mathcal J_i$ exactly when they contain one factor. Also $V(\mathcal J_i\mathcal O_{T_i})=b_i^{-1}V(\mathcal J_i)$, since extension is generated by the images of the ideal. Its image lies in $V(\mathcal J_i)$. Conversely, any $t\in V(\mathcal J_i)\setminus V(\mathcal I_i)$ has a unique preimage under $b_i$ by [thm-nagata-global-blowup-complement], and that preimage lies in the extended zero set. Points in $V(\mathcal I_i)$ are already in the first summand. Consequently $V(\mathcal I)=V(\mathcal I_i)\cup b_i(V(\mathcal J_i\mathcal O_{T_i}))$, without requiring $b_i$ to be surjective on the centre.

source.place: Tag 080A and the support hypothesis of Tag 080I, lemma-strict-transform-composition-blowups

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-strict-transform-composition] with first ideal $\mathcal I_i$, second ideal $\mathcal J_i\mathcal O_{T_i}$ and product ideal $\mathcal I$. Its isomorphism and support hypotheses were checked in steps 1 and 2. It identifies $W_i^{\mathcal I}$ with the strict transform of $W_i^{(i)}\to T_i$ along $q_i$. By [thm-nagata-strict-transform-is-blowup] this latter scheme is the blowup of $W_i^{(i)}$ in the extension of that second ideal. Since $W_i^{(i)}\to T_i$ is flat, [thm-nagata-blowup-flat-base-change], with its comparison [def-nagata-blowup-flat-base-change-map], identifies this blowup with $W_i^{(i)}\times_{T_i}T^b$. The comparison to the ordinary fibre product is the one with the two structure projections [def-nagata-strict-transform-blowup-comparison]; The flat-base-change comparison has the same first projection and the same lift to $T^b$: both lifts pull back the centre ideal to its exceptional invertible ideal, so uniqueness in [thm-nagata-blowup-universal-property] identifies them. Thus the two comparisons to the fibre product agree and the identification respects the closed inclusion and both projections. Flatness follows from [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-base-change], and local finite presentation from clause (3) of [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence].

Put $D=T\setminus V(\mathcal I)$ and $P=W\times_TT^b$. The strict transform is the scheme-theoretic image of the open part $P_D\hookrightarrow P$, by [def-nagata-strict-transform] and [def-nagata-scheme-theoretic-closure]. This inclusion is quasi-compact: on an affine open of $T$, $D$ is the finite union of the principal opens of generators of $\mathcal I$, and the inclusion is obtained from $D\hookrightarrow T$ by base change; use clause (3) of [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence]. It is quasi-separated, since the diagonal of an open immersion is an isomorphism. The opens $P_i=W_i\times_TT^b$ cover $P$. Apply [lemma-nagata-scheme-image-restrict-open] to each $P_i$: its restricted open part is exactly the one defining $W_i^{\mathcal I}$. Thus $W_i^{\mathcal I}=W^{\mathcal I}\times_PP_i$ as closed subschemes of $P_i$, with the specified inclusions. These are open subschemes covering $W^{\mathcal I}$.

Each point of $W^{\mathcal I}$ lies in one of the opens from step 4. Its local rings and its affine neighbourhoods there are also those in $W^{\mathcal I}$. Therefore [def-weil-flat-morphism] and [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], applied to the properties proved in step 3, give flatness and local finite presentation of $W^{\mathcal I}\to T^b$.

We verify the two global finiteness conditions separately. By [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence] (2), $W$ is qcqs since $g$ and $T$ are. By [thm-nagata-strict-transform-is-blowup], $W^{\mathcal I}\to W$ is the blowup of the extended finite-type ideal $\mathcal I\mathcal O_W$ (its generators are the images of local generators of $\mathcal I$). It is proper by [lemma-nagata-blowup-proper], hence quasi-compact by [def-weil-proper-morphism] and [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and quasi-separated by [lem-pc-separated-quasi-separated]. Thus permanence (2) gives that $W^{\mathcal I}$ is qcqs. The same argument for $T^b\to T$ gives that $T^b$ is qcqs. Permanence (1) now proves that the morphism $W^{\mathcal I}\to T^b$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Together with step 5 these are exactly the conditions for finite presentation in [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. No argument required density of $U$; only its inclusion in every ideal complement was used.
